1896: {A hole opening onto somewhere measurably worse, aimed at the formation | Aiming a hole is not a coherent operation and is what happens}. {four passes across everybody | nothing comes out and the aiming continues}.
1897: {Time is bent across the formation and their voices do not survive the bend | Speech occupies a duration and the duration is being deformed}. {a third lose their voice | they are speaking and the speech is elsewhere}.
1898: {A crack opened in the hour itself, above the formation | Hours are conventions and conventions can be fractured}. {seven in ten lose their voice | the crack is visible and is not in anything}.
1899: {One pulse of an age, delivered in the space of an exchange | An aeon is a duration with no agreed length}. {half of them are left with nothing to say | witnesses included, and the silence afterwards is documented}.
1900: {Open the way. Pay in blood, at the door, before the crossing | The Grand Grimoire specifies the blood and does not specify whose}. {a demon is admitted | the payment is made continuously, not once}.
1901: {Raise it, and then hold it up, which is the part nobody budgets for | Reanimation is easy and maintenance is the discipline}. {something dead stands and continues standing | your own blood is the scaffolding}.
1902: {Bind it while your reserve lasts. When the reserve ends, so does the binding | Elementals are not hostile and are not obedient either}. {an elemental joins the line | it goes when the funding does, without comment}.
1903: {Call downward. Nothing up there responds to small sums | Celestial hierarchies are ranked by what it costs to get their attention}. {something descends | it does not explain why it agreed}.
1904: {Start it. It runs on coin and continues running on coin | Automata were built for Renaissance courts and were mostly clockwork frauds}. {a machine begins operating | stopping the payments stops the machine mid-motion}.
1905: {Field the machine at a rate calculated by the hour and payable in advance | Mercenary artillery was hired the same way and bankrupted several cities}. {a war machine takes the field | the rate is ruinous and is stated honestly}.
1906: {The leash is removed and whatever is nearest answers | Domestic or wild is not specified and is not the operator's choice}. {your animal fights, or something else does | the wild does not send its best}.
1907: {Vermin answer promptly and feed on the caller while working | Payment in kind, drawn continuously}. {a swarm arrives and works | it does not distinguish the employer from the target}.
1908: {Something comes up out of the water and remains while the reserve holds | The water need not be nearby; it needs to exist}. {something aquatic joins the line | it returns when it is no longer being paid for}.
1909: {Call something winged downward onto the formation | Vertical arrival is the only advantage on offer and is sufficient}. {something with wings descends | it does not land}.
1910: {Something cold-blooded uncoils beside the caller without being introduced | Serpent convocation appears in every tradition and always requires a name}. {a serpent arrives | the name was given at some point and is not recalled}.
1911: {Root something growing into the field. It requires nothing and cannot remain | Plants convoked into unsuitable ground die on schedule}. {a growing thing takes root | it asks for nothing, which is unusual in this catalogue}.
1912: {Strike the bargain at the rate they always charge, which is not money | The small folk are not small and are not folk}. {they arrive and honour the terms | the rate is the usual one and is never itemised}.
1913: {A shade answers and is held upright by the shares it consumes | Shares burn at a rate the shade sets}. {a shade takes the field | it stops when the instrument is exhausted}.
1914: {The shadows nearby resolve into something with teeth in it | Resolution is the operative word; nothing is added}. {something toothed emerges from the dark | the shadows are shorter afterwards}.
1915: {Hold the way open. It cannot be propped and must be held | Holding costs continuously and cannot be delegated}. {something from outside comes through | letting go closes it, with whatever is halfway}.
1916: {Buy its attention. The tribute is due every turn and is not negotiable | Wyrms are creditors before they are creatures}. {a wyrm attends | missing a payment ends the arrangement immediately}.
1917: {Wake it. It will lean on the caller for the whole engagement | Waking something enormous is easier than supporting it}. {something enormous rises | the leaning is literal and is measured in reserve}.
1918: {Hire the champion by the turn, in advance, in coin | Condottieri were paid by the month and switched sides between payments}. {an armed champion fights for you | the contract is short and is honoured}.
1919: {Buy whoever is standing about with nothing better to do | The going rate for the unoccupied is very low}. {a crowd joins in | they are not good and there are several of them}.
1920: {Call something that eats money and keep supplying money | Mimics are appetite with a shape, and the shape is a container}. {something arrives and begins consuming | stopping the supply redirects the appetite}.
1921: {Burn the party's oil. Not coin, not blood, not reserve. Oil | The petrodemon is not balanced and has never claimed to be}. {a petrodemon is held on the field | it is bought outright, which is stated plainly}.
1922: {Ask something very old to attend. It will attend and it will drink | Age is the only quality that matters and it has all of it}. {something ancient takes the field | it drinks the caller dry and does not hurry}.
1923: {Call the creature you marked, from wherever it happens to be | The mark is the address and the address does not expire}. {the marked creature arrives | it is not pleased and it comes anyway}.
1924: {Call back the last thing the party put down, and pay in blood for it | The most recent death is the cheapest to reverse and the least willing}. {the last kill returns | it remembers who killed it}.
1925: {Call a marked person onto the field, where they stay for a few turns | Marked people can be called and cannot be kept}. {the marked person arrives | they leave shortly and are not consulted about either}.
1926: {A lesser copy of the caller, funded out of the caller's own reserve | Copies are always lesser; the shortfall is where the saving comes from}. {a diminished duplicate takes the field | it is worse than you and knows it}.
1927: {Call back a traveller the party has lost, by name, from wherever that is | The name has to be exact and the party has to agree on it}. {somebody who was lost returns | how long they stay is not disclosed}.
1928: {Mark the creature now so that a later rite can find it | Marking is cheap; finding is not}. {the creature carries the mark | it does not know and cannot remove it}.
1929: {Mark the person standing in front of you, at conversational distance | Consent is not part of the procedure and is not prohibited either}. {the person carries the mark | they can be called later, from anywhere}.
1930: {Send it away. Whatever it is, whatever it cost, it goes | Dismissal is the one working in this school that always succeeds}. {whatever is being held departs | nothing is refunded}.
1931: {The impostor settles on a face already at the table | Nothing about the copy is invented; every part of it is taken from somebody present}. {the borrowed name answers when it is called and the borrowed hands know the borrowed trade | what is handed back at the end is handed back only because it was never really taken}.
1932: {Two bodies are proposed and the flesh accepts both proposals | Chimerism happens in nature without ceremony and is found, when it is found, by accident}. {the limbs arrive in pairs that do not match and stay in pairs that do not match | there is no version of this that unhappens}.
1933: {The move that just landed is performed again, by the wrong body, at the body that performed it | Echolalia is the cheapest form of learning and the fastest}. {the technique arrives from the direction it came from | nothing about it has been understood, only repeated}.
